headline: Waymo expands robotaxi service to Sacramento and San Diego, adding 18 CA counties
summary: The California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) has approved Waymo's request to offer rides in new cities and expand its existing service across the San Francisco Bay Area and Los Angeles.
details: Waymo has received approval from the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) to significantly expand its robotaxi service. This decision allows the company to launch operations in Sacramento and San Diego for the first time. It also permits broader service coverage across the San Francisco Bay Area and Los Angeles.
The CPUC's approval follows a January filing by Waymo, which initially faced a suspension. These issues have since been resolved, paving the way for the service expansion.

The expansion will be gradual, guided by Waymo's safety framework, and will eventually cover 18 counties across northern and southern California. These include major areas like Alameda, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and San Diego.

Waymo previously announced intentions to expand into San Diego by November 2025 and Sacramento by February 2026. The approved fleet will include existing Jaguar I-Pace vehicles and new Ojai robotaxis, custom minivans built by Zeekr.
caption:
Waymo's robotaxi service is officially expanding to Sacramento and San Diego, plus more of the SF Bay Area and LA.

Waymo has received approval from the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) to significantly expand its robotaxi service. This decision allows the company to launch operations in Sacramento and San Diego for the first time. It also permits broader service coverage across the San Francisco Bay Area and Los Angeles.

The CPUC's approval follows a January filing by Waymo, which initially faced a suspension. These issues have since been resolved, paving the way for the service expansion.

The expansion will be gradual, guided by Waymo's safety framework, and will eventually cover 18 counties across northern and southern California. These include major areas like Alameda, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and San Diego.

Waymo previously announced intentions to expand into San Diego by November 2025 and Sacramento by February 2026. The approved fleet will include existing Jaguar I-Pace vehicles and new Ojai robotaxis, custom minivans built by Zeekr.
